key_insight: Open LLMs can only explain closed models when the surrogate measurements faithfully preserve the specific thing you want to study—prediction, attribution, or representation. The paper shows that log-odds are a practical API-compatible readout for binary classification, but fidelity depends on the level of analysis.
problem_solved: Mechanistic interpretability usually needs internal model access, but most deployed LLMs are closed and only expose limited API outputs like token log-probabilities. This paper asks when measurements from open models can be trusted as surrogates for claims about closed models.
method: Evaluates surrogate fidelity at three levels: prediction, attribution, and representation.
Uses binary classification as a setting where API-accessible log-odds can serve as a scalar proxy for model behavior.
Compares how well open-model measurements transfer to claims about closed-model internals under different interpretability tasks.
impact: This gives practitioners a principled way to know when open-model analysis is informative about closed LLMs. It can reduce wasted effort, improve interpretability workflows, and make API-based model auditing more scientifically defensible.
visual_elements: A three-layer stack showing prediction vs attribution vs representation fidelity

A side-by-side comparison chart of high-fidelity and low-fidelity surrogate cases

paper_title: Surrogate Fidelity: When Can Open LLMs Explain Closed Ones?
paper_authors: Philippe Chlenski, Zachariah Carmichael, Ayush Warikoo, Chia-Tse Shao, Yingxiao Ye
